name: TX-11
label: Safe R

key_factors: Strong Republican district with a -17 point partisan lean
Incumbent Pfluger has a massive financial advantage ($2.9M vs $47K cash)
Markets price Pfluger at 96% to win
No polling or expert ratings, but no evidence of Democratic strength
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Pfluger's incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising edge leave Reynolds with no visible path; markets price her win chance at just 3%. Nothing in the evidence suggests moving meaningfully off the fundamentals-based expectation of a double-digit Republican margin.
model.watch: A surprise influx of Democratic outside spending or a national wave environment could narrow the margin, though not plausibly enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
August Pfluger, the Republican incumbent, is heavily favored to win a third term in this West Texas district, which leans about 17 points Republican. He has raised nearly $3.2 million and holds $2.9 million on hand, while Democrat Claire Reynolds has raised under $90,000 with less than $50,000 available. No outside groups are opposing Pfluger, and no polls or expert ratings exist for the race.

Prediction markets give Pfluger roughly a 96 percent chance of winning. With no evidence of Democratic investment or polling strength, the race is rated Safe Republican, with an expected margin near 18 points.
